:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $b=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $b$ and points the same direction.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{b}{|\,b\,|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,b\,| & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{b}{|b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot [\begin{aligned}8 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 8\end{aligned}].$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $2a+b$ and points the same direction.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+b & =2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0+5 \\ 4+8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|2a+b| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169} \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $2a+b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(2a+b) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{13} \\ \frac{12}{13}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Let $n=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $n$ and points the same direction.
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{n}{|\,n\,|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|n| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{41}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $n$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{n}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{41}}\cdot n \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{41}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sqrt{41}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{41}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
